text_en: The words of the Teacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
text_cn: 达味之子耶路撒冷的君王“训道者”的语录：

text_en: Vanity of vanities, says the Teacher, vanity of vanities! All is vanity.
text_cn: 虚而又虚，训道者说：虚而又虚，万事皆虚。

text_en: What do people gain from all the toil at which they toil under the sun?
text_cn: 人在太阳下辛勤劳作，为人究有何益？

text_en: A generation goes, and a generation comes, but the earth remains forever.
text_cn: 一代过去，一代又来，大地仍然常在。

text_en: The sun rises and the sun goes down, and hurries to the place where it rises.
text_cn: 太阳升起，太阳落下，匆匆赶回原处，从新再升。

text_en: The wind blows to the south, and goes around to the north; round and round goes the wind, and on its circuits the wind returns.
text_cn: 风吹向南，又转向北，旋转不息，循环周行。

text_en: All streams run to the sea, but the sea is not full; to the place where the streams flow, there they continue to flow.
text_cn: 江河流入大海，大海总不满溢；江河仍向所往之处，川流不息。

text_en: All things are wearisome; more than one can express; the eye is not satisfied with seeing, or the ear filled with hearing.
text_cn: 万事皆辛劳，无人能尽言：眼看，看不够；耳听，听不饱。

text_en: What has been is what will be, and what has been done is what will be done; there is nothing new under the sun.
text_cn: 往昔所有的，将来会再有；昔日所行的，将来会再行；太阳之下决无新事。

text_en: Is there a thing of which it is said, “See, this is new”? It has already been, in the ages before us.
text_cn: 若有人指着某事说：“看，这是新事。”岂不知在我们以前早就有过。

text_en: The people of long ago are not remembered, nor will there be any remembrance of people yet to come by those who come after them.
text_cn: 只是对往者，没有人去追忆；同样，对来者，也不会为后辈所记念。

text_en: I, the Teacher, when king over Israel in Jerusalem,
text_cn: 我训道者，曾在耶路撒冷作过以色列的君王。

text_en: applied my mind to seek and to search out by wisdom all that is done under heaven; it is an unhappy business that God has given to human beings to be busy with.
text_cn: 我曾专心用智慧考察研究过天下所发生的一切；——这实在是天主赐与人类的一项艰辛的工作。

text_en: I saw all the deeds that are done under the sun; and see, all is vanity and a chasing after wind.
text_cn: 我观察了在太阳下所发生的一切：看，都是空虚，都是追风。

text_en: What is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is lacking cannot be counted.
text_cn: 弯曲的，不能使之正直，亏缺的，实在不可胜数。

text_en: I said to myself, “I have acquired great wisdom, surpassing all who were over Jerusalem before me; and my mind has had great experience of wisdom and knowledge. ”
text_cn: 我心里自语说：“看，我获得了又大又多的智慧，胜过了所有在我以前住在耶路撒冷的人，我的心获得了许多智慧和学问。”

text_en: And I applied my mind to know wisdom and to know madness and folly. I perceived that this also is but a chasing after wind.
text_cn: 我再专心研究智慧和学问，愚昧和狂妄，我才发觉：连这项工作也是追风。

text_en: For in much wisdom is much vexation, and those who increase knowledge increase sorrow.
text_cn: 因为，智慧愈多，烦恼愈多；学问越广，忧虑越深。
